question_text: Which sentence uses the subjunctive mood correctly?

options.text: I wish I was the department head.
I wish I were the department head.
I wish I am the department head.
I wish I be the department head.

hint_ladder.title: Ano Ba 'To?
hint_ladder.text: Subjunctive mood 'to. Ginagamit kapag wishful thinking, 'di totoo sa ngayon. Para kang sumisigaw ng 'Sana All!' sa loob ng exam room.

hint_ladder.title: The 'Sana' Rule
hint_ladder.text: Kapag 'I wish', ang susunod ay lagi nang 'were', hindi 'was' o 'am'. Parang automatic na sagot.

hint_ladder.title: Check the Subject
hint_ladder.text: Hindi mo kailangan baguhin ang 'were' kahit 'I' pa ang subject. Laging 'I wish I were'.

hint_ladder.title: Spot the Wrong Ones
hint_ladder.text: Siwas, gam, sam, be? Lahat sila mali. 'Were' lang ang tamang term pagkatapos ng 'wish'. Piliin mo 'yun.

A.text: You might have chosen A because 'I wish I was' sounds natural in everyday convo, but for wishes, the subjunctive requires 'were'.

B.text: Correct. After 'I wish', the subjunctive mood always uses 'were' for the verb 'to be'.

C.text: You might have chosen C because 'I wish I am' uses present tense, but 'wish' demands unreal 'were'.

D.text: You might have chosen D because 'be' appears in other subjunctive patterns, but after 'wish', 'were' is the only correct form.

next_time_rule: Remember: 'I wish I were' is the golden phrase. Whenever you express a wish, grab 'were'. It's like saying 'sana all'—formal and correct.
deconstruct_text:
Sitting in a barangay meeting, you hear someone say, 'I wish I were the captain.' That's the subjunctive mood—it shows a wish that isn't reality. In the civil service exam, they'll test if you can spot the correct 'were' instead of 'was' or 'am'.

Mental Trick: Isipin mong 'I wish I were' ay parang 'Sana All' na may fixed combo—like bagoong and kare-kare, never separate. Auto-complete in your head: after 'I wish', 'I were' agad.
